Action Plan:
1) Acute watery diarrhea with crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting:
   - Maintain hydration: increase clear fluids; start oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) obtained over-the-counter from pharmacy.
   - Symptomatic relief: use Paracetamol as needed for fever/pain (dose/route/frequency not discussed).
   - Diet: focus on clear fluids and soft foods (e.g., soup, mashed foods); gradually advance diet as tolerated.
   - Avoid alcohol until recovered.
   - Follow-up: if not improving within 48 hours or if signs of dehydration worsen, contact clinic for reassessment and possible further investigations.
2) Family history of colon cancer:
   - Noted father with stage III colon cancer; no acute action discussed today.
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: 3-day history of profuse watery, non-bloody diarrhea.
- HPI:
  - Diarrhea nearly every waking hour; watery, non-bloody.
  - Intermittent crampy lower midline abdominal pain, comes and goes; patient-rated approx. 6/10.
  - Nausea; some vomiting. Vomited after drinking milk; has been avoiding milk since.
  - Feels febrile/hot; no measured temperature.
  - Urinating less frequently than usual.
  - Able to take fluids; had lunch but stools remain loose.
  - Brother has had similar illness for ~5 days and is improving.
- Past medical history: Otherwise fit and well; no known chronic conditions reported.
- Medications: Paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented). No regular medications.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Father with colon cancer (reported as stage III).
- Social history:
  - Lives with mother and sister; brother does not live with patient.
  - Works in an office (government) in Central London.
  - Smoking: social use (occasionally, e.g., Fridays).
  - Alcohol: occasional beer on weekdays; heavier drinking 1–2 times per month.
  - Often buys food; does not usually eat with family.

Objective:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals or physical exam documented.
- No laboratory or imaging studies discussed or performed.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Acute watery diarrhea with crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis (High) — supported by abrupt onset, profuse watery non-bloody stools, crampy pain, subjective fever, and close contact with similar illness (brother). [DDx: “Acute viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus)” — High]
   - Differential diagnosis:
     • Acute bacterial gastroenteritis/foodborne illness (Medium): frequent watery stools, cramps, subjective fever; no blood lowers likelihood. [DDx — Medium]
     • Secondary (post-infectious) lactose intolerance/exacerbation with dairy (Medium): vomiting after milk in the setting of enteritis. [DDx — Medium]
     • Protozoal infection (Giardiasis) (Low). [DDx — Low]
     • Inflammatory bowel disease (Low). [DDx — Low]
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; if not improving within 48 hours or if dehydration worsens, patient to contact clinic for reassessment and possible further investigations (specific tests not discussed).
   - Treatment planned:
     • Oral rehydration: increase clear fluids; start Dioralyte (OTC oral rehydration solution).
     • Symptom control: Paracetamol as needed for fever/pain (dose/route/frequency not discussed).
     • Diet: clear fluids and soft diet (e.g., soup, mashed foods); gradual advancement as tolerated.
     • Avoid alcohol until recovery.
   - Relevant referrals: None discussed.
2. Family history of colon cancer:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Family history recorded; no acute concern driving current symptoms (DDx deems colorectal cancer unlikely in this acute presentation).
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable to current acute illness.
   - Investigations planned: None discussed today.
   - Treatment planned: None today.
   - Relevant referrals: None discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure), no physical exam, no objective hydration assessment, no travel/camping or recent antibiotic exposure queried, no stool red-flag review beyond blood (e.g., mucus, severe abdominal tenderness), no pregnancy status applicable, no medication reconciliation beyond Paracetamol, no documentation of weight loss or baseline weight.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted (no conflict).
- Transcript quality: Audio-only telehealth with some pauses/overlaps; overall intelligible but with occasional unclear/inaudible fragments; no measured vitals available due to telehealth format.
